section.h2: Frequently Asked Questions About Haemophilia A and B: Factor Replacement, Emicizumab, and Gene Therapy
section.intro: These FAQs explain how haemophilia A and B are treated today, from standard factor replacement and emicizumab to newer gene therapy options. All treatment choices should be guided by a qualified haematology team.

items.q: What is haemophilia A and B?
items.a: Haemophilia A and B are inherited bleeding disorders caused by a missing or reduced clotting factor. Haemophilia A involves low factor VIII, while haemophilia B involves low factor IX. Both lead to prolonged or spontaneous bleeding, often into joints and muscles. Severity depends on the remaining factor level, ranging from mild to severe. Diagnosis is confirmed through clotting factor assays and genetic testing, and management should be overseen by a specialist haematology team.
